sections.h2: What should a seller know about Whatcom County before dealing with property tax?
sections.html:
Whatcom County sits in the northwest corner of Washington, with British Columbia to the north and the Strait of Georgia on the west. It covers 2,503 square miles, of which about 16 percent is water, and the 2020 census counted 226,847 residents. Bellingham is the county seat and the largest city. The other incorporated cities are Blaine, Everson, Ferndale, Lynden, Nooksack and Sumas, and the county also includes Lummi and Nooksack tribal lands, Birch Bay, Point Roberts, Sudden Valley and Geneva.

The western lowlands are farmland and the east climbs into the Cascades toward Mount Baker. Agriculture is a big part of the economy, and the county produces most of the nation's raspberries. That mix means two neighbors a few miles apart can pay different tax rates, because each parcel sits in its own combination of city, school, fire and other districts. The numbers below come from the county's own pages.

sections.h2: Which Whatcom County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices matter to a homeowner, and each does a different job.

  • Assessor. Sets the value of every parcel as of January 1 of the assessment year (July 31 for new construction). Phone 360-778-5050. The Assessor also runs the senior and disability exemption program.
  • Treasurer. Bills and collects real and personal property tax, collects the real estate excise tax on sales, and handles tax foreclosure. The office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 311 Grand Avenue, Suite 104 in Bellingham, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Phone 360-778-5160. Drop boxes sit near the north rotunda entrance, outside the south entrance and outside the Treasurer's lobby.
  • Board of Equalization. Hears valuation appeals. It has three regular members and four alternates appointed by the County Council.

The Whatcom County Treasurer page lists online payment, tax lookup and foreclosure auction notices.

sections.h2: When are Whatcom County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Half is due April 30 and the other half October 31. The Treasurer sends the tax statement in February, and under RCW 84.56.020 a statement must go out by March 15 when the budget and levy steps are finished on time. When a due date lands on a weekend, the next business day counts. Mailed payments are judged by the post office postmark, not a postage machine date, so on the due date ask the counter clerk to hand-cancel the envelope.

Payments for taxes mail to Whatcom County Treasurer, PO Box 34873, Seattle, WA 98124-1873. Do not send other mail to that box. If your total is $50 or more you may pay in halves; the first half can also be paid late, with interest and any penalty figured on the full year, as long as it is paid by October 31.

Late taxes follow a statutory schedule:

  • Residential property with four or fewer units, including manufactured homes, carries 9 percent annual interest and no penalty.
  • Other property carries 12 percent interest, plus a 3 percent penalty on taxes still delinquent June 1 and another 8 percent on December 1.
  • A taxpayer may pay any delinquent year in full with interest and penalty without paying the current year first.
  • Real property foreclosure starts when the tax is three years delinquent. The Treasurer holds a tax foreclosure auction each November.

Income-qualified owners who live in the home may have remaining interest and penalties waived shortly before the three-year mark if foreclosure has been filed, once per property.

sections.h2: What are the property tax rates in Whatcom County?
sections.html:
There is no single county rate. The Assessor's 2026 report lists a levy rate per $1,000 of assessed value for every taxing district, and your bill adds up the districts that cover your parcel. The Treasurer's formula is assessed value divided by 1,000, times the combined rate. A sample of the 2026 rates:

Taxing district2026 levy rate per $1,000
State of Washington2.2445
County general0.7732
City of Bellingham1.3742
City of Lynden1.1102
City of Ferndale0.5917
Bellingham School District3.2828
Ferndale School District2.4081
Lynden School District2.5151

Source: Whatcom County Assessor, Assessor Report 2026. Fire districts, ports and other districts add more on parcels they serve.

The Assessor reports that countywide assessed value rose about 1.2 percent for 2026, and that most of the increase in tax bills comes from voter-approved measures rather than value growth. Every year staff physically inspect one-sixth of the county; area 5, which included mid-Bellingham, Geneva and Sudden Valley, was inspected in 2026 and area 6 comes in 2027.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Whatcom County assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition with the county Board of Equalization on the state form. Under RCW 84.40.038 the petition is due by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days after the value notice was mailed, or within a longer period of up to 60 days if the county legislative authority adopted one, whichever is later. For the 2025 assessment year the county posted an October 27, 2025 deadline, which has passed. Your Change of Value notice states the deadline that applies to you, so read it as soon as it arrives.

The Board must value property at 100 percent of market value and may lower, raise or keep the value. A late petition can be accepted for good cause such as serious illness, a natural disaster or postal delay. Appeals of the Board's decision go to the Washington State Board of Tax Appeals. Before filing, talk to an appraiser at the Assessor's office, because the Assessor values property at 100 percent of market value and can explain how your number was reached.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Whatcom County homeowners?
sections.html:
Two programs matter most for people selling under financial strain.

  • Senior and disability exemption. For 2026 taxes the prior qualifications still apply. A 2026 law change raises the income limit to $72,000 starting with 2026 income, which affects 2027 taxes, adds a standard deduction of $7,500 per person or $15,000 per couple, lowers the veteran disability rating that qualifies from 80 to 40 percent, and exempts participants from the state school levy in full. Three income levels, $54,000, $63,000 and $72,000, set how much assessed value is exempt from regular levies. Apply through the Assessor in person or online.
  • Destroyed property. After the December 2025 flooding, the Assessor lowered values on affected parcels in Sumas, Nooksack, Everson and Ferndale for the 2025/26 year. Values return to market for 2027 taxes. The Assessor's destroyed property coordinator handles claims for parcels that are still damaged.

Washington also runs a property tax deferral program under chapter 84.38 RCW, which each tax statement must mention. Ask the Assessor's office whether you qualify.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled when I sell a Whatcom County house?
sections.html:
Any transfer of property needs a real estate excise tax affidavit filed with the Treasurer, with payment, before the deed is recorded at the County Auditor. The Treasurer will not accept an incomplete affidavit or give legal advice on filling it out. You have 30 days from the date of sale before interest and penalty begin. Ask your escrow or title officer to request a payoff from the Treasurer for any delinquent years and the current half before the closing date.

Gift transfers also require a supplemental statement signed by both parties, and a minimum filing fee applies if no tax is due. Mobile homes have their own steps: one that will be moved needs a tax certificate from the Assessor and an orange decal from the Treasurer. For state rates and exemptions, see the Washington real estate excise tax page and the county's excise tax page.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Whatcom County?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day. Mailed payments count on the post office postmark date.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Whatcom County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest starts after the due date, 9 percent per year on a home with four or fewer units. Foreclosure begins once taxes are three years delinquent, and the Treasurer holds the auction each November. Income-qualified owners living in the home can ask about a waiver of interest and penalties.

faqs.q: How do I check what I owe in Whatcom County?
faqs.a: Use the Treasurer's online tax lookup or call 360-778-5160. Property tax records are public records. Ask for the payoff for each delinquent year as well as the current year if you are selling.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Whatcom County property value?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Board of Equalization. The deadline is stated on your Change of Value notice and is the later of July 1 or 30 days after the notice, or up to 60 days if the county set that period. The Assessor's office at 360-778-5050 can review the value with you first.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when a Whatcom County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays. The Treasurer collects it with an affidavit before the deed is recorded, and interest and penalty start after 30 days from the date of sale. Your escrow company normally takes it out of the seller's proceeds.
